session_cookie.name: __Host-pos_admin_session
session_cookie.description: The session cookie `POST /admin/login` sets: host-only, `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`, with a sliding idle TTL. A client does not read it — the browser presents it.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Two-factor sign-in, the session it issues, and the second-factor levers (ADR-0034, ADR-0060); an administrator's own sessions, listed and revoked; and who administers the console, by invitation, role and status (ADR-0067). An invitation's token and an enrolment's TOTP secret are each returned once and stored only as a hash or not at all. The last active owner cannot be demoted or suspended. Everything else on this surface stands behind the session these routes establish.

tags.name: config releases
tags.description: A release is one decision and many writes (ADR-0125): a named set of config publishes, aimed at a cohort or an explicit store list, timed once — in each store's own clock or at a single instant. Scheduling one expands it to a `scheduled_publishes` row per (node, store) pair, which ADR-0077's activator applies. These routes write no config versions of their own.

tags.name: store groups
tags.description: The cohorts a tenant publishes to as one, and their membership (ADR-0122). A group holds no configuration: publishing to one calls the same per-store publish once per member, so the config tree's four layers and the store's sync path are untouched. Membership is replaced wholesale under the group's own ETag, because a cohort is a set and a delta API merges two admins' concurrent edits into one neither of them chose.

tags.name: integrator access
tags.description: The credentials and destinations of the `/v1` integrator surface: a tenant's scoped API keys (ADR-0037) and the webhook endpoints a store's events are sent to (ADR-0032). A key's token and an endpoint's signing secret are each returned once, when it is made; no read returns either. A webhook URL is checked before it is stored, so it can never point into the cloud's own network. Revoking a key and deleting an endpoint are idempotent and say nothing about whether one existed.

tags.name: integrations
tags.description: The vendors this cloud can talk to, and what each needs (ADR-0153). Documented because it is the contract a fork's own console draws its connection forms from: the form is the provider's settings schema, so a console that hard-coded one vendor's fields would be wrong the day a second is added.

tags.name: reason codes
tags.description: The managed list a void, a discount, a comp, a refund, a drawer opening, a staff rejection, either cash movement and either stock correction must cite (ADR-0115, `docs/pos-spec.md` §11 item 2). Documented rather than deferred because it is a **fraud control**: a fork writing its own console needs to know that ids are server-minted, that an entry leaves service by going inactive rather than by being deleted, and that every write is conditional.

tags.name: devices
tags.description: What a store has actually admitted (ADR-0118). Documented rather than deferred with the rest of the device surface because it is the **only** read that answers it: a store admits tablets locally and offline, and until these events the cloud's picture of a store's tills was zero rows. Note the two identity spaces — the ids here are minted by the edge at pairing, and nothing joins them to the console-minted ids of `/admin/stores/{store_id}/devices`.

tags.name: box activation
tags.description: The device slots a store has, and how a box earns the credential for one (ADR-0050, ADR-0065, ADR-0148). An administrator registers a slot, then either issues a one-time activation code for its setup sheet or binds the code a box with no store shows on its screen. Either way the box receives its credential once, and only a hash of it is kept. An activation code is returned exactly once and can be cancelled until it is spent.

tags.name: device onboarding
tags.description: How a store's printers, kitchen displays and tills come into service (ADR-0041, ADR-0100, ADR-0112). A store proposes each device it discovers; an administrator approves it, stating how it is attached and which station it serves, or rejects it. A till is never discovered, so an administrator creates it directly. Nothing reaches a store until its approved devices are published as its `devices` node.

tags.name: printers
tags.description: What paper each approved printer takes and whether it cuts it (ADR-0160 decision 2), which printer a till's receipts go to and the languages they print in (decision 4), and the float a till's drawer opens with (ADR-0167 decision 4), the terminal whose print agent drives a printer (ADR-0112), and whether a cash drawer is wired to it (ADR-0165). A fork's own console needs to know that a printer nobody has set prints as 80 mm paper with a cutter, that a till nobody has set prints and opens its drawer as the store does, and that nothing reaches a store until its devices are published.

tags.name: media
tags.description: A tenant's image library (ADR-0042, ADR-0075): an upload is re-encoded into a bounded thumbnail and detail JPEG, the upload itself is never stored, and an item names an image by its id. A rendition never changes, so it is served with a long private cache.

tags.name: translations
tags.description: A tenant's translation grid (ADR-0020, ADR-0043): each content key to its strings by locale, every key carrying `en`, the fallback a till shows when a locale has none. The grid is one entity, replaced wholesale and conditionally from the grid screen, or merged row by row from a CSV after a dry run.

tags.name: till layout
tags.description: The buttons a till shows on each sales channel (ADR-0066): one per item per channel, under a display category, in a fixed grid slot or flowing by sort order. A publish compiles them into the store's layout, apart from its prices, so moving a button reprices nothing.

tags.name: modifiers
tags.description: The choices offered with an item (ADR-0066, ADR-0127): a modifier group offers some items on others, with how many a guest must and may pick. A group is tenant-wide; a publish keeps the groups a menu's channels can offer.

tags.name: tax
tags.description: What tax an item is charged (ADR-0074, ADR-0104): each item names a tax class, and the tenant's rate table gives each class a rate on each sales channel, in basis points, optionally broken into named components an invoice prints. The table is one entity, replaced wholesale and conditionally. A class that active items still use cannot be archived, and a store refuses to price an item on a channel its class has no rate for.

tags.name: menus
tags.description: Where a tenant's items are sold and for how much (ADR-0066): menus, which may inherit from a parent menu; their sections; and placements, an item on a menu with its price on each sales channel and whether it is available. Prices are integers in the currency's minor units, and they are T2, so reading placements needs `console.reports.revenue`. A placement's prices are the price-change journal: every change is audited with them. Nothing reaches a store until a menu is published to it, which compiles the menu with the menus it inherits from into the store's price book and till layout.

tags.name: catalog items
tags.description: A tenant's item master (ADR-0066, ADR-0075): each item's name and per-locale names, tax class, categories, course and photo. An item carries no price; a price belongs to its placement on a menu. Item ids are minted by the server and are what an order names an item by. The master round-trips as a CSV: export it, edit it in a spreadsheet, check the file with a dry run, then apply it. A file can update or create items but never mint an id. Nothing reaches a store until its catalog is published.

tags.name: catalog taxonomy
tags.description: How a tenant's catalog is sorted (ADR-0066, ADR-0130): item categories and their sub-categories, which reporting groups an item under; display categories and their sub-categories, which a till's layout shows; and courses, the order a table's dishes are served in. Ids are minted by the server, records are archived rather than deleted, and every edit is conditional on the version it was read at. An item category or sub-category that active items still use cannot be archived. Nothing reaches a store until its catalog is published.

tags.name: countries
tags.description: The read-only master data a console picks a store's country and locale from (ADR-0074, ADR-0105): the country modules this build carries, with the currency, number format, retention and till facts each fixes, and the content locales the platform serves. Fixed when the server starts.

tags.name: campaigns
tags.description: The promotions a tenant authors for its stores' pricing engine (ADR-0077): item, combo, bill, voucher and manual campaigns, and the codes a voucher campaign redeems. Ids are minted by the server and every edit is conditional on the version it was read at. Nothing reaches a store until its campaigns are published. A voucher code carries redeemable value, so even listing codes needs `console.campaigns.manage`, and no audit entry records a code or a discount's terms.

tags.name: reports
tags.description: What a store did over a window of its trading days, read from the materialised rollup and never from the event log (ADR-0036, ADR-0081): its activity counts, its takings, fees by code (ADR-0159) and tax by component (ADR-0168), each as a read or a CSV download, and the X or Z report for one day. Prices are T2, so every read or export of an amount needs `console.reports.revenue`; the activity counts need only `console.data.read`. An export is audited by how many rows it held, never what they held. Resetting a store's rollup has the projector rebuild it from the event log.

tags.name: fleet
tags.description: Where each store runs and how it is standing (ADR-0068, ADR-0110, ADR-0114): its last contact and whether it is online, the configuration and binary it runs, what it holds unsent, and whether the country its data rests in agrees with the one it is registered in. Online and current are derived when read, never stored. The one write answers a region difference, the compliance warning the single-store read shows.

tags.name: operations
tags.description: Whether the cloud and the fleet are working (ADR-0068, ADR-0073, ADR-0078): the alerts the evaluator keeps, fleet-wide, with their acknowledgement and resolution; the health of each background loop; and the reconciliation runs that show no store's events were lost.

tags.name: registry
tags.description: The organisation a console administers (ADR-0065): its tenants, the brands a tenant trades under, and its stores. Every record is created active with an id minted by the server and leaves service by being archived rather than deleted; every edit is conditional on the version it was read at. A new tenant is given its six starting roles (ADR-0158). A store's devices, configuration and reports are separate surfaces under the store's path.

tags.name: subject requests
tags.description: The instrument the Data Protection contact uses to carry out one data subject's access, portability or erasure request under Vietnam's PDPD (Decree 13/2023) or the GDPR (ADR-0076). It assists that process and records it; it does not decide it. Before any of these routes is used, a person confirms the lawful basis and the subject's identity, and confirms consent, retention and, for customer analytics, a DPIA. A request from an EU resident is escalated to the Data Protection contact rather than actioned here, and moving an export across a border needs a DTA or explicit consent first. Each route acts on one subject of one tenant: there is no list, no bulk export and no cross-tenant read, because a bulk export is an escalation, not a feature. Only an owner holds `console.subjects.manage`, and every call is audited with ids and counts, never a personal value.

tags.name: audit
tags.description: Every console write, who made it and when (ADR-0069), read by any console role. An entry records ids, codes and statuses, never a person's name or a secret; an employee's staff code is shown only to a role that may read the roster (ADR-0158 decision 9).

tags.name: settings
tags.description: Every value a store may run differently (ADR-0160, `docs/configuration.md`). A value is written once, at the tenant, a brand, a store group or one store; each store runs the most specific value that reaches it, and every store a write reaches is republished in the same request. Documented because a fork's own console draws its settings screen from the catalogue here.

tags.name: people
tags.description: Who may do what at a store (ADR-0070, ADR-0158): the people a tenant employs, the roles that say what each may do, the assignments that give a person a role at one store, a store group or every store, and the publish that compiles them into a store's `permissions` node. Staff records name people, so reading them needs `console.people.read`; the permission catalogue and the roles name nobody. A write is audited with ids, codes and statuses, never a name or a PIN. Archiving a person or a role, removing an assignment, and assigning to a group or every store publish to every store the change reaches before they answer, and report each store's outcome. The readiness read names roles and counts people, and names no person.

tags.name: fees
tags.description: The charges a bill adds — a service charge, a packaging fee, a delivery fee (ADR-0159). A rule is written once, at the tenant, a brand or one store; for each fee a store runs the most specific rule that reaches it, and every store a write reaches is republished in the same request. An item list may name item categories, which are compiled into items when the store is published. Documented because a fork's own console draws its fee screen from these routes, and needs to know that a store which cannot apply a rule is left as it is rather than sent part of its list.

tags.name: lease
tags.description: Which machine is the store (ADR-0108, ADR-0110, ADR-0114): the store's lease generation, issued only by the server and only by a bump, which is the act of making a different machine the store and may move where it runs and where its data rests. A bump will not abandon a previous machine that still holds events unless a person acknowledges it by generation. A handover ends when the old machine drains, or when a person settles it by attestation; retiring the old machine afterwards is a separate decision. Every one of these is audited with who made it.

tags.name: ota rollout
tags.description: Which release a store installs, and when (ADR-0052, ADR-0078): the rollout names a hosted release, the lowest eligible ring and how much of the fleet ring may take it, and the key it is signed by; the placement puts the store in a ring and fixes its place in the ramp. Both are configuration-tree nodes the store pulls, validated by the rules the store itself applies. The kill switch halts or resumes a rollout without restating it. Writes are audited.

tags.name: release hosting
tags.description: The signed releases the cloud hands its stores (ADR-0088, ADR-0141). An operator uploads a release executable with its minisign signature, or has the cloud fetch them from the published release. The cloud stores the bytes and never signs them or checks the signature: each store verifies it itself. A release, once hosted for a target, keeps its bytes. A Windows store's one-file installer is a hosted executable named for that store. Served only where the cloud is configured to host artifacts.

tags.name: scheduled publishes
tags.description: Publishes waiting for their time (ADR-0077): a store's pending ones, listed, and one cancelled before it is applied. Each names the node it will publish and its instant, and the scheduler publishes it then. A cancel is audited.

tags.name: floor
tags.description: A store's floor (ADR-0072): its areas and the tables in them, each with a label, seats and a place on the editor's grid, archived rather than deleted, and every edit conditional on the version it was read at. Nothing reaches the store until its floor and kitchen are published together. The printable QR sheet mints each active table's signed token, which carries no personal data.

tags.name: kitchen
tags.description: A store's kitchen (ADR-0072): its stations, each with a backup, a late threshold and the language its tickets print in, and the rules that route a menu item or a course to a station. A rule matches exactly one of the two, and only a course the tenant carries. Stations are archived rather than deleted and edited conditionally; a rule is removed. Nothing reaches the store until its floor and kitchen are published together.

tags.name: inventory
tags.description: A tenant's inventory (ADR-0079): its ingredients, each in a unit of measure; its suppliers; and a recipe for each menu item or modifier that consumes them, with an auto-86 threshold. Ingredients and suppliers get ids minted here; a recipe is keyed by the item it makes. Every edit is conditional on the version it was read at. A recipe's amounts are proprietary, so no audit entry records them. Nothing reaches a store until its inventory is published.

tags.name: openapi
tags.description: This document (ADR-0019), served without a session: it describes routes and carries no tenant data.

tags.name: config nodes
tags.description: The per-store configuration a console reads and writes one node at a time (ADR-0057, ADR-0080, ADR-0111, ADR-0145): the sales channels a store takes orders on, the payment methods it accepts, the second origins its edge answers, its QR ordering guardrails, how long it keeps a synced event, its delivery-marketplace policies, its locale, its legal identity, its tax table and its capability flags, and a preview of any node's publish. A read gives the node as the store runs it, composed from all four layers; a publish writes it on the store's own layer as a new configuration version, which the store pulls on its next sync.

tags.name: config
tags.description: A store's configuration tree (ADR-0033): four layers — tenant, brand, store and device — composed and validated into the document the store runs, with an append-only history of versions. A layer is replaced whole, conditional on the version it was read at; a rollback restores a past version as a new one. The effective document is redacted for its reader, and the per-node read carries no values at all, only which nodes exist and when each was last published. A store pulls a new version on its next sync.
